prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a downward-angled view of a flat, muddy ground plane in frames 1–4 that transitions in frame 5 to an upright view of a fenced yard with a continuous distance gradient from the foreground (0.3–1 m) out to the background fence and trees (over 10 m away). In frame 1, the camera wearer's raised right hand is brightest and within arm's reach at about 0.3–0.5 m on the lower right, partly occluding one of two dogs standing side by side at 1–1.5 m on the left (one facing up toward the camera wearer, the other at the bottom left edge partly out of view), while in frame 2 both dogs stand about 0.3 m apart at 1–1.5 m facing away and downward. By frame 3, one dog remains near the bottom center at 1 m (partly cropped at the lower edge) while the second dog has retreated to about 2–2.5 m Ahead and to the right, facing away to the upper left. In frame 4, the camera wearer's two hands holding a green bag and leash hardware appear in the lower foreground within 0.3–0.5 m, and in frame 5 a person stands on the left at roughly 3–4 m facing right in profile (not looking at the camera wearer) with a small dog far to the right near the fence at 8–10 m. The depth map clearly separates the foreground hands and dogs from the dark, low-contrast mud background that blends together in RGB, though it is unreliable in frame 4 where the white chair at the left edge and distant feet at the top edge are completely smoothed into the ground plane, and in frame 5 where the chain-link fence disappears into the ground gradient.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against the unsegmented fenced yard, detecting nothing in frames 1, 2, and 4, two animals in frame 3, and two distant figures in frame 5. In frame 3, it locates the closer dog at the bottom center (about 1 m away, partly out of view at the bottom edge) and the further dog to its upper right (about 2–2.5 m away, roughly 1–1.5 m behind and right of the first dog, both facing away from the camera wearer). In frame 5, it segments the standing person on the left at 3–4 m facing right in profile with their arms at their sides (within their own reach, not looking toward the camera wearer) and a tiny shape at the far right edge about 8–10 m away near the fence. This map highlights the exact silhouette of the standing person against the overexposed sky and trees in frame 5 and flags the tiny far-right figure that is nearly invisible in RGB. However, it is highly unreliable across the sequence: it completely misses both dogs and the camera wearer's occluding right hand (at 0.3–0.5 m) in frames 1–2, misses the camera wearer's hands, green bag, white chair, and distant feet in frame 4, mislabels the two dogs in frame 3 as 'bird' and 'bear', and mislabels the distant dog at the right edge of frame 5 as 'person'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1–4 and detects only a single yellow body skeleton in frame 5, corresponding to the person standing on the left side of the fenced yard about 3–4 m from the camera wearer. The skeleton's aligned left-side shoulder, hip, knee, and ankle keypoints, along with head keypoints shifted to the right of the torso line, show that the person is standing upright in right-facing profile, looking across the yard to the right rather than toward the camera wearer, with their right wrist hanging down beside their hip within their own arm's reach. In frames 1–4, as the camera tilts down toward the ground where two dogs move from 1–1.5 m away (frames 1–2) to 1–2.5 m away (frame 3) and the camera wearer's own hands enter the lower foreground at 0.3–0.5 m (frames 1 and 4), no body or hand skeletons are rendered. The pose map makes the standing person's exact limb articulation, upright posture, and profile orientation in frame 5 clearer than the washed-out RGB coat sleeve, and avoids false body detections on the dogs. However, it is unreliable for egocentric hand tracking because it completely fails to detect the camera wearer's raised right glove in frame 1 and both gloved hands manipulating the green bag and clasp within arm's reach at the bottom of frame 4, as well as the cropped person's legs at the top edge of frame 4.
